unit.title: Angles
unit.blurb: Acute, right and obtuse angles, estimating and measuring with a protractor, and angles on a straight line.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Classify, estimate and measure angles in degrees, including acute, right and obtuse angles.

O2.t: Know that angles on a straight line add up to 180° and use this to find missing angles.

p: Angles are measured in **degrees (°)**. A **right angle** is 90°. An **acute** angle is less than 90°. An **obtuse** angle is between 90° and 180°.
To **estimate**, compare with a right angle: is it smaller or bigger? Then measure with a **protractor**.

lesson.t: Why we use the right scale on the protractor
p: A protractor has two scales. Starting from 0° on the arm we line up decides which scale to read.

lesson.q: One arm of an angle is on the 0 of the inner scale. The other arm passes 130 (outer) and 50 (inner). The angle is acute. What is it?
steps: We started from 0 on the inner scale

p: Put the centre of the protractor on the vertex.
Read the scale that starts at 0 on that arm.
Longer arms do not make a bigger angle. The angle is the amount of turn.

p: Angles that sit together on a **straight line** add up to **180°** (a half turn).
If one angle is 70°, the other is 180° − 70° = **110°**.

lesson.t: Why angles on a line make 180°
p: A straight line is a half turn. Two right angles make a straight line, so the angles on one side of a line add up to 180°.
